subject.title: Feature: Telegram Reactions - Two-Way Support with Prompt Guidance

question: Should Telegram use the existing `reactionLevel` plus `reactionNotifications` to control inbound prompt guidance, or introduce a separate public `reactionGuidance` setting with independent defaults?
rationale: The existing controls already partially own this behavior, while incoming reactions currently do not guarantee an agent turn; choosing a permanent config and execution contract cannot be resolved safely as a mechanical implementation detail.

options.title: Compose Existing Controls
options.body: Use `reactionLevel` for outbound guidance and inject restrained inbound soft-signal guidance only when `reactionNotifications` permits delivery, without adding another config key.

options.title: Add Independent Guidance
options.body: Introduce and document `reactionGuidance: off|minimal|full`, including explicit precedence, generated metadata, upgrade behavior, and interaction with both existing controls.

options.title: Keep Outbound Guidance Only
options.body: Retain current behavior and decline standardized inbound emoji semantics until reaction-trigger and persistence policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Compose Existing Controls
recommendation.body: Use `reactionLevel` for outbound guidance and inject restrained inbound soft-signal guidance only when `reactionNotifications` permits delivery, without adding another config key.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the original reaction feature and are already connected to the product-level issue discussion.
